newsitem.title: UK: Brazilian real at true level -- central banker.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian real at true level -- central banker.

text.p: The level at which Brazil's currency is now trading is a true reflection of its value while maintaining exchange rate stability remains the priority, a senior central bank official said on Tuesday.

Asked how long Brazil's industrial exporters could withstand both high interest rates and a strong real, Gustavo Franco, director of international affairs at Brazil's central bank, said the current level was about right, and that exchange rate stability was the important issue.
"The exchange rate now is the true value," he told a conference of investors in London.
"It's important to have external equilbrium -- to keep offering competition to industry, to deepen ties with the international commmunity and to bring new technology into the country."

Some analysts have been arguing that an overvalued real is largely responsible for weakness in exports of industrial goods -- those exports most sensitive to exchange rate fluctuations -- over the first nine months of this year.

But Kleinwort Benson analysts calculate that the real is overvalued only by about 5.0 percent in purchasing power parity terms and that productivity and efficiency are more to blame for the industrial export weakness.
"If you measure the exchange rate now using wholesale prices and compare it with one month before the stablisation plan, there is only a 7.0 percent appreciation," Franco said.
"But if you compare it with the price of first class restaurants in Sao Paulo it is a different situation," he added.
"The question is a relative one -- it is a question of maintaining Brazil in a situation of external equilibrium."

He declined to give a forecast either for Brazil's monthly or annual trade deficit, which is starting to worry financial markets after a much larger than expected trade gap emerged in September, and after one of the lowest export volumes this year was recorded in the third week of October.
Franco said only that the trade deficit was usually wider in the final quarter of the year due to seasonal or extraordinary factors.
